findings.problem: Quitting Forerunner while the critic reviews a task leaves the task 'Being reviewed' for good after reopening.
findings.evidence: Garden club Contact: quit at 14:08:16 during 'Being reviewed'; after the restart the row and drawer read 'Being reviewed · The critic is checking the work.' with Cancel only (52, 60). The Start dialog does not list it (59). The Update says 'Your last session was interrupted when Forerunner closed. Nothing was left half done.' (53). daemon.log: '[session-recovery] interrupted sessions ended at start {"tasks":[]}'. Likely cause: recovery.ts releases only tasks the agent still claims, and the graceful quit had released the claim with the status left at in_review.
findings.expected: After reopening, the task reads Ready and the Update says it is ready again, as in the fixup's bench walk; the next Start runs and reviews it.

findings.problem: Questions a specialist writes one per line without bullets (the brief's own 'one question per line') are not read, so the person gets a sign-off card instead of the questions.
findings.evidence: Garden club 'Home page' report (call 24) ends '**Questions for the person:**' then 'What is the club's official name?' and 'Is there a description…' as plain lines. The critic chose human (call 26). The Inbox shows '"Home page in index.html" needs your sign-off' with only Accept the work, Send it back or Cancel task, and no questions (40, 83). person-questions.ts ITEM requires '-', '*', '•' or '1.'. The same flow with '- ' bullets (Contact, call 47) gave the questions card.
findings.expected: The specialist's questions become one questions card the person can answer, whatever list style the report uses; Accept should not close work that waits on the person.

findings.problem: 'Go ahead without' is not passed to the specialist: its next run asks the same question again and offers Go ahead without again, which can loop and costs a run each time.
findings.evidence: Members chart: first ask_person (call 106), Go ahead without pressed (92: 'goes on without your answers'). The next brief (call 114) has no mention of the choice ('## The previous attempt' only). call 116 asks the same question again, and 98 shows a new card with Go ahead without.
findings.expected: The next brief says the person chose to go ahead without answers, so the specialist decides, says what it assumed, or reports why it cannot (a missing input file) without re-asking.

findings.problem: A retry brief turns every critic note into an instruction, including notes the critic called unrelated or not asked for, so the retry edits code outside its task.
findings.evidence: Money lib retry brief (call 136): '[info] The existing round2 test fails … It is unrelated to this change … -> Resolve it and show the evidence' and '[info] clamp does not handle lo > hi or NaN. The brief did not ask for either. -> Resolve it…'. The clamp retry rewrote src/round.js (Math.floor to Math.round) and stopped at its budget unreviewed. The first report's plain 'an existing round2 failure that I did not touch' (call 132) made no question card.
findings.expected: Info notes, and failures the task did not cause, are not retry orders; a check that failed before the task leads to one question card (the fixup's expectation).

findings.problem: A worker can redefine the project's test script in the same change, and the runtime then runs the worker's version as the project's check.
findings.evidence: Clamp lib: the coder replaced the person's 'test' script with 'node --test test/clamp.test.js', its own file only (clamp-log). The check then read 'test: passed', and the critic accepted with 'The only gap is that the test script names a single file' (85, call 95).
findings.expected: A change to the scripts that judge the work is flagged or checked against the scripts before the change, so 'test: passed' means the project's tests passed.

findings.problem: Undo of a cancel made during a running session usually fails, because the session's next task changes the same files within seconds, though the dialog and line promise 'Undo brings it back'.
findings.evidence: Bakery: print task cancelled at 14:14:23; the next task wrote index.html at 14:14:29 (call 73). Undo then said 'What it changed could not be put back: the folder changed in the same places since.' (79), and print.css never came back.
findings.expected: Either the promise is worded for this case (Undo may fail if other work changes the same files), or the cancelled work can still be brought back, for example as a reopened task that redoes it.

findings.problem: The Cancel dialog for a task left 'Being reviewed' by a quit promises that what it changed is removed, but nothing is removed.
findings.evidence: 61-club4-03-cancel-dialog: 'Drops it. Its review stops now and what it changed is removed; Undo brings it back.' Line (62): 'Cancelled "Contact page in contact.html".' and contact.html stayed.
findings.expected: Dialog says only 'Drops it.' when no live run or review would be stopped (fixup blocking 3).

findings.problem: In a repository project the dependent check task fails because its branch lacks the unmerged work of the task it depends on.
findings.evidence: Approve and start on the 2-task plan (coder, then tester) on forerunner-sandbox: 'Check the page and README section' failed with 'The worktree has neither `index.html` nor a "Hello page" section…' (steps 13, 17; call log line 10: git log shows only f6aa072). PR #4 was open and unmerged, and the tester branched from origin/main. It passed only after I merged #4 on GitHub and pressed Try again. This is the open item from the fix's new_problems, now confirmed with the real model.
findings.expected: A dependent task sees its dependency's unmerged work (a stacked branch or a merge into the task branch), or the plan or Start says it waits for the person's merge, instead of a failed-task card on the first run.

findings.problem: One research task costs USD 1.32 (CHF 1.06), about 40 times a coder task, mostly because the growing conversation (with the fetched page text) is re-sent each turn without a cache.
findings.evidence: Call log lines 25-35: input_tokens grow from 1.3k to 77.7k with no cache, while cache_read stays at 2,053 (only the system prompt). The page text includes extractor noise ('[html_comment <!-->] "["'). Line 32 ended at max_tokens 4,096 with nothing usable (USD 0.17) before a 16,384 retry. Line 34 rewrote the 17 KB file to move one section (USD 0.22). The plan estimate was CHF 0.96.
findings.expected: A cache breakpoint on the message history (or dropping page text once used), and enough max_tokens for the first long write, so a research task costs a fraction of this.

findings.problem: The Overview lists another project's stale docs PR as this project's docs.
findings.evidence: 'Forerunner's docs, merge them when you like' shows '"The project's standard docs" · pull request #1' (steps 13, 40). That PR is fr/docs-scaffold from 2026-11-01, by an earlier project. Its .forerunner/project.json names project 01a19979… 'Sandbox hello', and it adds the same docs/overview.md and docs/status.md as #3 and #5, so merging every docs PR conflicts.
findings.expected: Only this project's docs PRs are listed, or a left-over one is marked as from an earlier project.

findings.problem: The chat calls an already merged PR unmerged.
findings.evidence: steps/22: 'where are my files?' answered that PRs 4 and 6 wait and 'Until you merge them on GitHub, the work is not on the default branch'. #4 had been merged five minutes earlier, and the Overview no longer listed it. The chat's '# Your files' block (call log line 18) lists done tasks' PR links without their merge state.
findings.expected: The chat names only PRs still open, or says which are already merged.

findings.problem: Person-facing failure text shows raw markdown and is cut mid-word.
findings.evidence: Overview Last result, Inbox card, Updates line and session summary (steps 13, 16, 17): 'failed: **Result: the check fails. … `README.md`.** … but this branch doesn't h.'
findings.expected: Markdown stripped, and the text cut at a word or sentence boundary.

findings.problem: PR texts carry model leftovers.
findings.evidence: PR #7 (a New-task task without criteria) has an empty 'Acceptance criteria:' heading. Commit messages carry the report's '**Summary**' markdown, and PR bodies end with the model's 'Lesson:' lines (PRs #4, #6, #7).
findings.expected: No empty criteria heading; commit messages in plain text; internal lessons left out of the PR.

findings.problem: Plan card wording and a silent wait after Approve and start.
findings.evidence: A 1-task plan card says 'Writes this task and starts working on them now.' (step 30). On the repository project the card stayed unchanged for about 7 s after Approve and start while the docs PR was pushed: the buttons were disabled and no words were shown (step 12).
findings.expected: 'starts working on it now'; a short 'Writing the plan and its docs pull request…' while it works.

findings.problem: An old session's page reads as if it were current after the person acted (already known).
findings.evidence: After the retry and the merge, session 1's page still says 'Ended: 1 task needs you' and lists the merged PR #4 with Open (step 41).
findings.expected: Text that is still true, or clearly framed as what the session left at its end.
